highlights.title: SpaceX IPO Filing: The Key Numbers
highlights.description: SpaceX filed publicly for what stands to be the largest-ever initial public offering, revealing billions in losses and a super-voting share plan allowing Elon Musk to keep the company under his control. The rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence giant has reported a net loss of $4.28 billion on revenue of $4.69 billion for the first quarter. Some investors remain doubtful whether the sum of Musk’s aspirations for SpaceX are worth valuing at as much as $2 trillion. Bloomberg's Charlie Well

SpaceX pitches itself as integrated interplanetary proto-monopolist in IPO filing

highlights.title: Nvidia says it has ‘largely conceded’ China’s AI chip market to Huawei
highlights.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company has "largely conceded" China's advanced artificial intelligence chip market to Huawei.

highlights.title: In SpaceX’s IPO, Elon Musk is a risk factor
highlights.description: The SpaceX IPO is here, and it's more than just an historic public offering that could make Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire. It also reveals more ways in which Elon Musk's companies interact and overlap with each other, shuffling money around in ways that are often difficult to keep track of. This is evident in ways that are both obvious and less so. A CTRL-F search for "Tesla" yields 87 results, xAI is mentioned 356 times, and X 267 times. Even the Boring Company (7 times) and Neuralin

highlights.title: SoftBank Group shares soar 20% as Nvidia earnings signal strong AI momentum
highlights.description: SoftBank Group is closely tied to the AI boom through its stake in Arm Holdings, whose chip designs are used in AI servers and data centers powered by Nvidia systems.

highlights.title: SpaceX IPO Requires Leap of Faith in AI, Mars and Musk’s Vision
highlights.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX pulled back the curtain on a business empire that has racked up ballooning losses and debt after acquiring a cash-hungry startup, and pumping billions of dollars into futuristic endeavors ranging from AI to a Mars rocket.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang says he’s found a ‘brand new’ $200B market for Nvidia
highlights.description: The next big thing for Nvidia will be CPUs for AI agents, $200 billion worth, CEO Jensen Huang predicts.

highlights.title: AMD Commits More Than $10 Billion to Taiwan AI Investments
highlights.description: Advanced Micro Devices Inc., the leading challenger to Nvidia Corp. in AI computing chips, pledged to invest more than $10 billion in Taiwan to expand partnerships and add packaging capacity.

chips_cloud.title: Nvidia Targets New Revenue Engine Beyond Hyperscalers
chips_cloud.description: Nvidia beat analysts’ estimates with its latest results and forecast, and used its latest quarterly report to tout progress in diversifying the company. Though investment in artificial intelligence has continued to surge from large data center clients, Nvidia predicted that a vast array of other businesses and governments would soon become a bigger source of revenue. Bloomberg's Neil Campling reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
